docs.title: What is xztrainer
docs.text: It is just a minimalistic PyTorch training loop implementation using open-source packages such as torchmetrics and accelerate to tackle with all the heavy lifting. No complex ecosystem, no bloatware, no "what the hell does that 5k lines of code function do?". Read the docs (and optionally code), implement what you need and start making fun training your models.

docs.title: 1. Install xztrainer
docs.text: Run pip install xztrainer torch torchmetrics accelerate or poetry add xztrainer torch torchmetrics accelerate depending on package manager you use.

docs.title: 2. Set up Accelerate
docs.text:
Since xztrainer uses Accelerate, you need to configure the training setup.

  • To save configuration globally - just launch accelerate config and specify parameters for your training setup.
  • To save configuration locally - same as above, but also specify --config-file argument: accelerate config --config-file .accelerate

docs.title: 3. Write your training script
docs.text: See an example here.

docs.title: 3.1. Prepare
docs.text:
Specify some preparation steps in your code, such as locking random seeds and enabling TF32 computations. See xztrainer utilities docs.

from xztrainer.setup_helper import set_seeds, enable_tf32

set_seeds(0xCAFEBABE)
enable_tf32()

docs.title: 3.2. Implement your Trainable
docs.text:
You need to implement your custom training logic by inheriting from a XZTrainable class.

Trainable is used for:

  • forward pass code, including loss computation;
  • specifying what metrics you want to calculate while training (xztrainer uses torchmetrics for updating and calculating the metrics since it supports distributed metric computation out of the box, see torchmetrics docs);
  • specifying some other callbacks, such as model loading callback or logging callback

Use xztrainer trainable docs to see full list of functions you can implement in your Trainable.

An example that uses cross-entropy loss for an image classification model, calculating accuracy as a metric:

from xztrainer import XZTrainable, BaseContext, DataType, ContextType, ModelOutputType
import torch
from torch import nn
import torchmetrics

class SimpleTrainable(XZTrainable):
    def __init__(self):
        self.loss = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()

    def step(self, context: BaseContext, data: DataType) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[str, ModelOutputType]]:
        logits = context.model(data['image'])
        preds = torch.argmax(logits, dim=1)
        loss = self.loss(logits, data['label'])

        return loss, {'predictions': preds, 'targets': data['label']}

    def create_metrics(self, context_type: ContextType) -> dict[str, torchmetrics.Metric]:
        return {
            'accuracy': torchmetrics.Accuracy('multiclass', num_classes=10)
        }

    def update_metrics(
            self, 
            context_type: ContextType, 
            model_outputs: dict[str, ModelOutputType], 
            metrics: dict[str, torchmetrics.Metric]
    ):
        metrics['accuracy'].update(model_outputs['predictions'], model_outputs['targets'])

docs.title: 3.3. Create standard PyTorch objects
docs.text: You need to implement your standard PyTorch objects related to working with data. And, for sure, your model object.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
An example dataset that remaps standard torchvision CIFAR10 dataset from tuple-yielding to dictionary-yielding just for convenience.

import torch
from torch.utils.data import Dataset
from torchvision.datasets.cifar import CIFAR10
from torchvision.transforms import ToTensor

class CifarDictDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, train: bool):
        self.base_data = CIFAR10(root='./cifar10', download=True, train=train, transform=ToTensor())

    def __getitem__(self, item):
        image, label = self.base_data[item]
        return {
            'image': image,
            'label': torch.scalar_tensor(label, dtype=torch.long)
        }

    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.base_data)

docs.title: Collator
docs.text:
An example collate function that stacks images and labels

import torch

class CifarCollator:
    def __call__(self, batch: list):
        return {
            'image': torch.stack([x['image'] for x in batch], dim=0),
            'label': torch.stack([x['label'] for x in batch], dim=0)
        }

docs.title: Model
docs.text:
We will just use resnet18 model from torchvision.

from torchvision.models.resnet import resnet18

model = resnet18(weights=None, num_classes=10)

docs.title: 3.4. Create training configuration
docs.text:
You need to create a configuration for the trainer.

Use xztrainer trainer documentation to see what parameters you can configure.

Example:

from xztrainer import XZTrainerConfig
from torch.optim import AdamW
from torch.optim.lr_scheduler import OneCycleLR

config = XZTrainerConfig(
    experiment_name='exp-2',
    minibatch_size=32,
    minibatch_size_eval=256,
    epochs=10,
    optimizer=lambda module: AdamW(module.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4),
    gradient_clipping=1.0,
    scheduler=lambda optimizer, total_steps: OneCycleLR(optimizer, 1e-3, total_steps),
    save_steps=100,
    dataloader_persistent_workers=True,
    dataloader_num_workers=8,
    log_steps=10,
    eval_steps=500,
    collate_fn=CifarCollator()
)

docs.title: 3.5. Initialize Accelerator object
docs.text:
Since xztrainer uses Accelerate internally, you need to create an Accelerator object.

Use Accelerator documentation to see what parameters you can configure here.

Example with gradient accumulation and TensorBoard logging:

from accelerate import Accelerator

accelerator = Accelerator(
    gradient_accumulation_steps=32,
    log_with='tensorboard',
    project_dir='./training-logs/'
)

docs.title: 3.6. Start training
docs.text:
Instantiate XZTrainer instance with all the objects you created before and call train(...) function.

Use xztrainer trainer documentation to see what happens inside train(...) function.

Example:

from xztrainer import XZTrainer

trainer = XZTrainer(
    config=config,
    model=model,
    trainable=SimpleTrainable(),
    accelerator=accelerator
)
trainer.train(train_data=CifarDictDataset(train=True), eval_data=CifarDictDataset(train=False))

docs.title: 4. Run your training script using Accelerate
docs.text:
• If running a Python module - accelerate launch -m mymodule.train or accelerate launch -m mymodule.train --config-file .accelerate if you have a local configuration file
  • If running a Python script - accelerate launch mymodule/train.py or accelerate launch mymodule/train.py --config-file .accelerate if you have a local configuration file

docs.title: 5. Explore saved artifacts
docs.text:
Inside a project_dir you specified in a Accelerator configuration, you will see:

  • Saved checkpoints inside checkpoint directory
  • In case of logging enabled (log_with parameter for Accelerator) - logging artifacts in runs directory

docs.title: cut_model_outputs(context, model_outputs, remainder)
docs.text:
Function used to cut out model_outputs based on a remainder value.

Since accelerate repeats some last samples in both validation and training datasets (let's call these samples "padded samples") to ensure batches are split across GPUs evenly in distributed setups, you may want to cut out these padded samples before metric calculation.

Default implementation just doesn't do anything because it does not know model output artifacts structure.

If you doesn't implement this function, you may see a slight difference between calculated metrics for a distributed and non-distributed setups.

Examples:

>>> return {'predictions': model_outputs['predictions'][:-remainder]}

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default context BaseContext

Current train/evaluation context

required model_outputs ModelOutputsType

Model output artifacts

required remainder int

Number of last samples that are padded samples and need to be cut out.

required

docs.title: Configuration Object
docs.text:
Training setup is configured using a XZTrainerConfig dataclass object.

Below is a list of properties you can configure.

docs.title: xztrainer.model.XZTrainerConfig dataclass
docs.text: A configuration for XZTrainer training setup

docs.title: collate_fn: t.Callable[[list[object]], t.Any] = default_collate class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: A function used to collate multiple dataset items into a single batch.

docs.title: dataloader_num_workers: int = multiprocessing.cpu_count() class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Number of worker processes used for data loaders.

docs.title: dataloader_persistent_workers: bool = True class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Boolean value indicating whether to keep workers alive after each epoch.

docs.title: dataloader_pin_memory: bool = True class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Boolean value indicating whether to pin memory for data loaders.

docs.title: dataloader_shuffle_train_dataset: bool = True class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Boolean value indicating whether to shuffle a training dataset within a dataloader.

docs.title: epochs: int instance-attribute
docs.text: Number of epochs to train for.

docs.title: eval_steps: int = 0 class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
Controls frequency of running a model on evaluation set.

Can be either:

  • -1 - to disable evaluation

  • 0 - to evaluate only after an epoch finishes

  • Any positive value - to evaluate at each Nth training step

docs.title: experiment_name: str instance-attribute
docs.text: Name of current experiment. Used for logging and checkpoint saving

docs.title: gradient_clipping: float = 1.0 class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Max gradient norm used for gradient clipping. Can be set to 0 to disable gradient clipping.

docs.title: log_steps: int = 100 class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
Controls frequency of logging model metrics.

Can be either:

  • -1 - to disable logging

  • 0 - to log only after an epoch finishes

  • Any positive value - to log at each Nth training step

docs.title: logging_level: t.Union[int, None] = logging.INFO class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Logging level that xztrainer initializes Python loggers with. Set to None to make xztrainer not do anything with Python loggers.

docs.title: minibatch_size: int instance-attribute
docs.text: Minibatch size used for training. In case of a multi-gpu or gradient accumulated train setup, it is a physical batch size for a single GPU.

docs.title: minibatch_size_eval: int instance-attribute
docs.text: Minibatch size used for evaluation. In case of a multi-gpu or gradient accumulated train setup, it is a physical batch size for a single GPU.

docs.title: optimizer: t.Callable[[nn.Module], Optimizer] instance-attribute
docs.text:
A callable that creates an Optimizer object from a Module object. Module object can be used to pass its parameters to Optimizer constructor, for example.

Examples:

>>> optimizer=lambda module: AdamW(module.parameters(), lr=1e-3, weight_decay=1e-4)

docs.title: save_keep_n: int = 3 class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Number of saves to keep while training. After a new save finished, all the other saves will be deleted except for save_keep_n last ones. Set to -1 to disable save removal.

docs.title: save_steps: int = 100 class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text:
Controls frequency of saving a model and trainer state.

Can be either:

  • -1 - to disable saving

  • 0 - to save only after an epoch finishes

  • Any positive value - to save at each Nth training step

docs.title: scheduler: t.Callable[[Optimizer, int], LRSchedulerProtocol] instance-attribute
docs.text:
A callable that creates a Learning Rate Scheduler object from an Optimizer and total number of training steps.

Examples:

>>> scheduler=lambda optim, total_steps: transformers.get_linear_schedule_with_warmup(optim, int(0.1 * total_steps), total_steps)

docs.title: skip_nan_loss: bool = True class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Boolean value indicating whether to skip update when a NaN loss value occurs.

docs.title: tracker_config: dict[str, t.Any] = field(default_factory=dict) class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Arbitrary hyperparameters logged to experiment tracker.

docs.title: tracker_init_kwargs: dict[str, t.Any] = field(default_factory=dict) class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Arbitrary keyword arguments used for Accelerate experiment tracker. Directly passed to accelerator.init_trackers(...). See Accelerate docs

docs.title: tracker_logging_dir: t.Optional[str] = None class-attribute instance-attribute
docs.text: Logging directory (or remote address) for Accelerate experiment tracker. If None - it will be set to {project_dir}/runs automatically.

docs.title: train(train_data, eval_data)
docs.text:
This function:

  1. Prepares all the objects used for further training, such as optimizer, dataloaders, metrics, learning rate scheduler, logger.
  2. Wraps these objects using accelerator.prepare(...)
  3. If a training checkpoint exists - loads it and initializes all the previously prepared objects from it.
  4. Prints out total parameter count used for training
  5. Trains for N epochs, where N specified in trainer config
  6. While training, the trainer can save its state, run evaluation and log metrics, - it is specified in trainer config.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default train_data Dataset

Dataset used for training

required eval_data Optional[Dataset]

Dataset used for evaluation. Can be None to disable evaluation.

required
